claim: Daily medians are a slow level plus noise, so a smoothed level beats the last value as the centre.
failure_mode: centre no better than last value
prediction: Median of last k days lowers pinball loss on noisy series.
refuted_if: Point error of the smoothed centre is above the last value's.
result: Loss-weighted error ratio against the last value 1.6 (h=1), 1.2 (h=3), 1.1 (h=7) on the 37 scored series; no mean reversion on afhubbard.

claim: A series that changed recently is more likely to move again; conditioning the change distribution on that state improves intervals.
failure_mode: interval width ignores state
prediction: State-conditioned pooled changes beat drift.
refuted_if: No gain over pooled changes without state.
result: mix with state chgk3: +0.072 over drift [+0.054,+0.086]; with recency +0.081 [+0.057,+0.093] (dev headline, 4,278 cells). Validation alone +0.028 [-0.006,+0.051], not significant; in a blend with gbm +0.069 [+0.051,+0.083].

claim: Per-series change quantiles are noisy on short histories; pooling by collector and class fixes it.
failure_mode: drift falls back to flat on short histories (42% of baseline loss)
prediction: Pooling raises skill mainly where drift has under 20 samples.
refuted_if: No gain on short-history cells.
result: +0.045 over drift [+0.036,+0.059] overall, 0.150 against 0.153 on cells where drift is live: pooling fixes the fallback and nothing more (dev headline, 4,278 cells).

claim: Jumps in a median come from provider-mix changes and partly revert.
failure_mode: large moves (9% of cells, 61% of loss)
prediction: Composition jumps revert, repricing jumps persist.
refuted_if: Reversal slope of composition jumps not below zero.
result: Composition jumps mostly do not revert: slope of the next 7-day change on the jump -0.16 (90% CI -0.30 to -0.14, n=56); exited offers return within 7 days in 5.6% of 162 fastgpu exits and 0 of 118 gpurentalprices exits. Repricing: momentum on fastgpu (+0.40 at h=3, CI 0.19 to 0.77, n=124), reversion on gpurentalprices (-0.46 at h=7, CI -0.69 to -0.19, n=256) driven by marketplace asks. Dev offer rows to 2026-10-13.

claim: The trailing day of some collectors is provisional and later revised.
failure_mode: anchor value wrong
prediction: Anchoring on the day before the origin helps.
refuted_if: n/a
result: The pack holds one data vintage.

claim: Pretrained time-series models carry no usable signal on administered step-like prices.
failure_mode: centre and width
prediction: Zero-shot quantiles lose to drift.
refuted_if: Zero-shot beats drift.
result: Supported for the centre, refuted for the width. Raw quantiles: Chronos-Bolt -0.050, TimesFM -0.055 against drift. Last value as centre with the model's width: +0.055 and +0.061 (dev headline, 4,278 cells); on validation Chronos width +0.121 over drift [+0.071,+0.157], the best single method.

claim: Other collectors' series for the same GPU lead a given series.
failure_mode: centre no better than last value
prediction: Lagged cross-series changes add skill at h=3 and h=7.
refuted_if: No gain from the partner's last change.
result: Shifting the centre by the partner collector's last change: every beta at or below the base (dev headline, 4,278 cells).

claim: The share of a collector's series that changed recently predicts how far each series moves next.
failure_mode: upper tail under-covered at h=7
prediction: +0.005 to +0.02 pooled skill.
refuted_if: No alpha in {0.25,0.5,1} with CI above zero.
result: Every variant at or below the base mix (dev headline, 4,278 cells).

claim: After a one-day move above 5% the price gives back part of the jump within 7 days.
failure_mode: large moves
prediction: Weak; CI includes zero.
refuted_if: CI excludes zero on the negative side.
result: rev 0.15: -0.001; rev 0.3: -0.003 against the base (dev headline, 4,278 cells).

claim: A burst of dated price-increase headlines (Exa, one published day per search) precedes upward jumps.
failure_mode: upper tail under-covered at h=7
prediction: +0.005 to +0.02 pooled skill at h=7.
refuted_if: No g with 90% CI above zero.
result: g=0.5: +0.0096 against the base, 90% CI [-0.004,+0.015]; 13 origins helped, 21 hurt; nearly all gain from 5 origins in one episode (dev headline, 4,278 cells).

claim: Every median jump is a repriced offer near the middle of the panel or a change in panel membership.
failure_mode: large moves
prediction: Composition share of jumps is material.
refuted_if: Causes cannot be attributed from the panel.
result: Median reproduced from offers on 100% of 2,483 series-days. 579 changes since 4 Aug: 86% repricing, 10% composition, 4% mixed (an independent count by the panel agent on 33 series: 84%, 6%, 10%). Share of the blend's dev loss: composition 32%, mixed 22%, Verda's steady increases 17.5%, one marketplace ask series 8.9%, hyperscaler spot 6.8%. A composition jump equals the panel's one-offer fragility (correlation 0.88, n=60); its new value is a neighbouring order statistic or midpoint in 79% of cases at h=1 and 54% at h=7. 60 composition events fall on 19 dates.

claim: Simulating the offer panel and recomputing the median beats scaling the last value by empirical log changes.
failure_mode: q50 loss equals the last value's; upper tail under-covered
prediction: First method with q50 loss below the last value's.
refuted_if: Panel model at or below mix on dev.
result: Panel simulator v1 (per-offer hazards, pooled symmetric reprice sizes, hl=14): dev skill 0.170, +0.001 against mix [-0.024,+0.057]. Blend with mix 0.180, +0.011 against mix [-0.002,+0.040]. q50 loss 0.997 of the last value's alone. Upper tail at h=7 unchanged (25% above q90). Reachability alone (v0) loses: -0.162. Why: up-moves over 5% in which a brand-new offer entered are 115 cells and 31% of last-value loss on the 33 panel series; entry happens on 1-2% of panel-days and cannot be simulated from the panel's own history. Not nominated.

claim: Large provider repricings are announced in public before they appear in the price data.
failure_mode: large moves
prediction: Unknown; either answer is a finding.
refuted_if: Under 20% of top events have a dated public source before the move.
result: 2 of 37 top repricing events (5%, 4% of their loss weight) had a dated public announcement before the move: Nebius (Reuters and others 16-17 Sep, effective 1 Oct, lead 15 days) and Jarvislabs (24 Sep, effective 5 Oct, lead 10 days). 23 of 37 events are marketplace asks with nothing to announce. On rate cards 2 of 12 events, 37% of rate-card loss weight. The keyword rule fired on 4 of 10 no-event controls (CI 19-65%; rule written after two earlier versions fired on 10 of 10). Exa Snapshot is not on our plan, so a published date does not prove the text is unchanged (two pages carry later-dated entries). Exa spend $1.56.

claim: The upper-tail gap at h=7 is a stable miscalibration that online recalibration fixes.
result: The upper-tail gap at h=7 is one multi-week regime, not a stable bias: above-q90 rate 0.110 in the first half of dev and 0.330 in the second (weekly 0.13, 0.02, 0.08, 0.24, 0.38, 0.38, 0.29, 0.08; lag-1 autocorrelation of the daily rate 0.93). Conformal q90 correction on mix: +0.023 [+0.008,+0.031] overall but -0.006 in the first half and +0.030 in the second; on the three-mix ensemble +0.008 [-0.003,+0.014]. Adaptive conformal inference loses (-0.017 to -0.025). Lower-tail correction adds nothing. Not nominated.

claim: Online weights learned from realised pinball loss beat equal-weight blending.
result: Best learned combiner (rolling 14-day constrained stacking, shrunk halfway to equal weights): +0.0037 against equal weights over 11 experts, 90% CI [-0.002,+0.007]; best of a 60-config grid, 4 of which beat equal weights. Equal weights over the 11 experts score 0.183, above every single expert (best 0.169). The best expert changes inside dev (pretrained widths 0.24-0.25 in the first half, 0.12-0.13 in the second); learners that chase it lose up to 0.02 (follow-the-leader -0.021). Decision: equal weights.

claim: Move probability is predictable from state and a hurdle model converts it into skill.
result: Whether a price moves is predictable (AUC 0.825 out of sample on 4,038 headline dev cells; 0.747 from the series' own past move rate), direction is not (AUC 0.54; 0.49 at h=7). As a forecaster the hurdle model loses: 0.108 against mix 0.169 (-0.061 [-0.097,-0.040]); no blend weight beats mix. Its size distributions on active cells are 1.6 times wider than mix's and the lower tail leaks (q10 loss +0.03 to +0.04 of total). LightGBM stage 1 is overconfident. So most of the 0.219 hindsight bound is rankable but not convertible with these size distributions; the 0.226 direction bound is out of reach from these features.

claim: A text decision model (Laya) reading a price history classifies up/flat/down better than logistic regression.
result: Laya 0.4.32 (421M) on 3,000 held-out cells, lower/unchanged/higher: log loss raw 1.851, temperature-refit 1.105, with class bias 0.812, against base rate 0.760, logistic regression 0.562, LightGBM 0.491 (AUC move vs no move 0.29 against 0.90-0.91). A logistic layer on Laya's outputs reaches 0.635, still behind logistic regression on the raw numbers with the same rows (0.609). Fine-tune not completed (the run exceeded memory). LightGBM probabilities as a forecaster: 0.099 against mix 0.165 on the held-out origins; base rates shifted (up-moves 16% in train, 46% in test on headline).

claim: Pretrained widths transfer across periods because they react to volatility in the context window; group context and covariates add to them.
result: Pretrained width is a recent-volatility tracker: elasticity of Chronos width to 14-day volatility 1.02 and to long-run volatility -0.10 (mix: 0.53 and 0.31). Shorter context is better (512: 0.144, 64: 0.147, 32: 0.156, 16: 0.162 on dev). Chronos-2 with group context and covariates no better (0.146). Best: Chronos-Bolt-small, 16 days, lower level 0.15: dev 0.167 alone (-0.002 against mix); blend with mix 0.190, +0.021 [+0.010,+0.044], both halves positive. Validation query 8: blend 0.170 against mix 0.112, +0.058 [+0.039,+0.080], one-sided p<0.001. Kept.

claim: An unusually wide level gap between collectors for the same GPU closes, predictably.
result: Pair-gap closing slope at h=7 +0.005 per unit z, CI [-0.002,+0.007], n=1,904 (19 origin dates only). No centre shift lowers q50 loss (own level gap shift 0.5: -0.031 skill). Compute Screener, GIX, gpueconomy, GetDeploying, cheapest series, AWS spot: no usable signal on dev (several have under 4 distinct values in the window). One borderline width skew from the median's position between p25 and p75: +0.006 [0.000,+0.010], gains in 3 of 8 weeks; one of about 18 variants. Not nominated.

claim: Weights written by a frontier model into a tiny net match or beat the same net trained by gradient descent.
result: Tiny net (579 parameters, zero weights reproduce mix exactly). Writer GPT-6 Astra kept 4 of 8 hand-written edits (17 non-zero weights, 17 of 40 forward passes); each kept edit beat its sign-reversed and random-direction controls. Held-out half of dev: hand-written weights beat the same net trained by Adam (+0.094 [+0.084,+0.123]) and random search (+0.022 [+0.019,+0.024]), but the gain over mix includes zero (blend 0.172 against mix 0.169 on full dev 0.174). Nearly all benefit came from one rule: widen the upper tail when the offer panel leaves room above the median.

claim: Nearest-neighbour analogs from the whole pack beat a binary state.
result: Dev (orchestrator re-run): analog {pool all, k 600, drop n14 and sign} 0.199, +0.030 against mix [+0.009,+0.061]; blend with mix 0.200, +0.031 [+0.017,+0.053], positive in both halves (+0.034 [+0.005,+0.070], +0.030 [+0.015,+0.056]). Validation query 6 (13-30 Oct, headline, 1,816 cells, declared before running): blend 0.134 against mix 0.112, +0.022 [+0.007,+0.043], one-sided DM p=0.031; gain at h=7 (+0.015) and h=3 (+0.007), on fastgpu (+0.013) and gpurentalprices (+0.011). Upper-tail exceedance at h=7 on validation 9%. Kept, pending the false-discovery correction over the round's queries. The feature drop was chosen on dev; with all features analog alone is negative in the first half of dev.

claim: An in-context tabular model beats boosted trees on the small pooled training set.
result: Stopped by the orchestrator at 12:10 PT before a full dev score: the machine was thrashing (load above 100 on 15 cores, swap full) with 19 agents, and this was the heaviest job with the lowest expected gain (boosted trees on the same features give +0.053 over drift, below mix). Not a result about the method.

claim: An activity gate (zero width for series that do not move) lifts skill on the full posted rental set.
result: Routing by class over-fits (rules picked on early origins: 0.20 early, 0.09-0.11 late, below mix 0.140). The activity gate alone carries over: zero width when a series has not moved in 14 days, one fixed forecaster elsewhere. Gate over three mix variants on rental_all, late origins: 0.148, +0.008 against mix [+0.002,+0.016]; headline +0.005 [+0.002,+0.011]. Named after seeing late results (lightly selected). hyperscaler_list stays below the last value (-0.041).

claim: Giving each offer its provider's own recent signed repricing dynamics, with the order statistics doing the capping, predicts centre and tails better than pooled symmetric reprices.
failure_mode: q50 loss equals the last value's; large moves
prediction: First q50 loss clearly below the last value's on series whose middle offer belongs to a dynamic provider.
refuted_if: At or below mix on dev, or the gain is in one half of dev only.
result: prov {L 1, W 21, gate dyn}: each offer follows its provider's recent signed daily changes; the median of the simulated panel stops at the static neighbour. Dev (orchestrator re-run): 0.208, +0.039 against mix [+0.013,+0.087]; q50 loss 0.95 of the last value's overall and 0.90 where the middle provider is dynamic (first method below 1). First half +0.009 [-0.007,+0.029], second +0.046; with W 14 the first half is negative. Symmetric sizes lose (0.142). Validation query 7: blend with mix 0.185 against mix 0.112, +0.072 [+0.059,+0.087], one-sided p<0.001; gain at h=7 +0.051, fastgpu +0.047, gpurentalprices +0.026. Kept. Untested: a reversal of Verda's uptrend (none in dev).

claim: The repricing state of the provider at the middle of the panel is a sharper forecast state than the series' own recent changes.
failure_mode: interval width; regime change when the middle offer changes hands
prediction: Beats mix, mostly through tighter intervals on static-middle series and wider ones on dynamic-middle series.
refuted_if: No gain over mix with the 90% CI above zero.
result: Middle-provider reprice bucket as the conditioning state: 0.167 against mix 0.169 (-0.002 [-0.014,+0.027]); blend with mix +0.008 [-0.001,+0.027]. The state separates quiet from active cells but the dynamic buckets hold about 100 past cases at late origins, too few to price up-jumps (up-moves over 5%: 0.032 against mix 0.047). The same information works when simulated (prov, H24) and not when used as a lookup key. Not nominated.

claim: A provider's published pricing policy, found by Exa in pages dated before the origin, predicts how often its posted price moves.
failure_mode: no prior for providers with thin history
prediction: DYNAMIC-labelled providers reprice far more often; label beats the pooled rate as a prior under 14 days of data.
refuted_if: AUC of the label against measured rates near 0.5.
result: Policy label from Exa (pages dated on or before 2026-08-17): reprice rate DYNAMIC 0.156 [0.04,0.30] (10 units), FIXED 0.048 (22), UNKNOWN 0.073 (24 of 56, because most pricing pages are undated). AUC against a 15% rate 0.79 [0.66,0.93] with 5 positives; it mostly restates spot against rate card. Verda's own 5 Dec 2025 post says dynamic pricing is being phased out, yet its rate card reprices on 41% of days. As a prior under 14 days of history a constant zero (error 0.057) beats the label (0.070) and the pooled rate (0.086). Labelling was not blind for 11 providers. Exa spend $1.05.

claim: Announced repricings with an effective date, collected by Exa into a calendar, can be applied to the offer panel exactly and remove the error on those moves.
failure_mode: large rate-card moves (2 of 12 top events, 37% of rate-card loss weight, were announced 10-15 days ahead)
prediction: Announced prices match the panel on the effective date; calendar-adjusted centre removes most last-value error on affected cells.
refuted_if: Panel prices do not change to the announced price on the announced date.
result: Exa calendar (463 searches, $2.83, end dates on or before 2026-11-06, 500 tracker hits dropped unopened): 8 dated announcements, 6 ahead of time. Panel check on dev: 17 of 17 checkable offers moved to the announced price exactly; date error 0 days on gpurentalprices, +1 on fastgpu. Inside the provider simulator (prov with cal on; orchestrator re-run): dev 0.283 against 0.209 without it, +0.074 [0.000,+0.100]; all of it from two events in the second half (Nebius effective 1 Oct, Jarvislabs 5 Oct); on the 100 changed cells skill 0.154 to 0.489 and q50 loss 0.53 of the last value's; the 4,136 other cells are bit-identical. The collector lag was read off the same two events, so this is an in-sample upper bound. It cannot be checked on validation: no announced change takes effect in a panel during 13 Oct to 6 Nov. Sunday window: Lambda +15% effective 2026-11-16 (published 2026-11-06), after every scored target.

claim: Tails shaped by the panel's one-offer-out and one-offer-in medians, weighted by the composition hazard, cover composition jumps better than smooth scaling.
failure_mode: composition and mixed cells (54% of blend loss; composition cells run at 0.88 of last-value loss)
prediction: Lower loss on composition cells on both tails without raising loss on no-move cells.
refuted_if: Dev gain under 0.005 or loss rises on no-move cells.
result: fragility {mode mix, boost 20, bkind any} over mix: tails get mass at the origin-day panel's one-offer-out and one-offer-in medians; the membership hazard is raised for a provider that changed any of its other series in the last 3 days (measured on dev: 0.102 chance of another entry or exit within a day against a base of 0.0036, 28 times). Dev (orchestrator re-run): 0.192, +0.023 against mix [+0.011,+0.045], halves +0.049 and +0.018; composition cells' loss ratio 0.94 to 0.84; cost on no-move cells -0.012. Validation query 9: 0.219 against mix 0.112, +0.107 [+0.052,+0.152], one-sided p=0.008; h=7 +0.084, fastgpu +0.090. Kept. On dev it adds little on top of mix + fm2 + analog + prov (0.2133 to 0.2164 as a fifth member). The boost was chosen on dev.

claim: H100 and A100 rental prices decay with age at a rate estimable from the last 12-18 months, giving a usable 2-3 year projection.
failure_mode: long-horizon view
prediction: Decay model beats no-change on a one-year backtest.
refuted_if: No-change wins the backtest.
result: Backtest failed: no-change beat the decay model on 117 weekly-median series (log error 0.42 against 0.66, difference CI +0.18 to +0.30) and on AWS spot (0.30 against 0.67, 20 cells). Every on-demand median rose 15-82% a year over the last 12 months (shortage regime) while multi-year AWS spot fell 31%/yr (H100) and 9.5%/yr (A100). Conditional projection, GetDeploying on-demand median: H100 3.83 now, 1.67 (0.76-3.78) at +24 months; A100 1.80 now, 1.51 (0.72-3.17) under decay or 0.45 (0.17-1.15) under per-unit-of-work parity. Older chips rent at a premium per unit of work (A100 2.30x, H100 1.78x of B200/B300), shrinking 21%/yr and 13%/yr. Income-approach resale: H100 about 16k USD (10k-25k), A100 about 8.8k (5k-14k); published asks fall inside.

claim: Panel entries and exits are predictable from the provider's footprint elsewhere (same GPU on the other collector, other GPUs on the same collector, recent entries into other panels), and the entry price from its price elsewhere.
failure_mode: up-moves over 5% with a new entrant: 115 dev cells, 31% of last-value loss on panel series
prediction: At least one flag lifts the daily entry rate several-fold; entry price error from the reference well below the pooled entrant distribution.
refuted_if: No flag lifts the entry rate by a useful factor, or the wrapper does not beat prov on dev in both halves.

claim: The three kept changes removed loss from the causes they were aimed at (dynamic repricing, thin panels), and what remains is dominated by membership changes and unannounced one-off repricings.
failure_mode: iteration 2 residual
prediction: Loss on dynamic-provider cells falls most from the earlier blend to the current one; entrant and unannounced one-off cells dominate the residual.
refuted_if: Loss by cause shrinks uniformly, or the residual is dominated by width cost on no-move cells.

claim: The provider simulator stays ahead of the reference model if a dynamic provider's trend stops or reverses after the origin.
failure_mode: untested regime: no reversal of Verda's uptrend in dev
prediction: Loses at short horizons, keeps an edge at h=7 because neighbouring static offers cap the error.
refuted_if: prov falls below mix pooled under a synthetic stop or reversal.
result: Synthetic counterfactuals on 534 second-half dev cells (future path of the middle dynamic provider replaced): prov minus mix +0.040 actual, +0.033 trend stops, +0.035 reverses at trailing speed, +0.035 mirrored. Loses on Verda at h=1 by about 4% of loss, keeps 13-15% at h=3 and h=7. A 50/50 blend with mix keeps about 75% of the edge. Also fixed: simulation order depended on Python's hash seed (now deterministic, 0.2089). Marketplace panels: not letting absent offers return adds +0.009 [0.000,+0.016] on one series; not adopted in the validated configuration.
